note:
Ring presets — THE COMPOSITIONAL RING MODEL (owner decree 2026-08-05): one entry = one dial styling, {name, outer, letters}. 'outer' names a config.constants.RING_OUTERS entry directly (bot_cross/top_cross/hexa/cross/full/octa) — it resolves the empty hour fields the letters stand in; no more guessing a 'layout' from a positions signature. Each of the FIVE bundled presets below is LOCKED to exactly one outer (constants.RING_OUTER_LOCK, enforced by data.rings.validate_preset): DOMY=bot_cross, LOOP=top_cross, Dollar=hexa, Templar=cross, The One=full — a custom ring (Settings) may pick ANY outer freely. The preset's INNER band and, for custom rings, its own CROWN TEXT are Settings-level choices, not card fields (constants.RING_INNER_PRESET_DEFAULT / RING_INNER_DEFAULT). Adding an entry here (or a custom one in Settings) is all a new styling needs. 'letters' pair with the outer's own positions by index and come from the letter library (RING_LETTER_FILES). 'The One' seats just Ω at 24h on its locked 'full' outer's single empty field (the full outer plate is otherwise solid); 'Templar' seats four templar-cross glyphs on its locked 'cross' outer's four empty fields. Optional 'triangle' (the 'hexa' outer only, ROADMAP 15b): overrides hexa's own metal triangle so a 6-letter preset can split into two 3-letter metal groups instead of hexa's own plain single finish on all six; on Dollar this override only actually APPLIES when the owner's per-preset 'Two metals' toggle is on (settings.ring_two_metals / app.controller._ring_two_metals) — off, the preset falls back to one finish on all six exactly like a card with no triangle at all. Optional 'legend': hour(as the position int) -> {name, reading} — the per-letter HOVER LEGEND (owner: what a letter stands for), quoted verbatim from CANON.md's Banknote table; each reading may carry a second '

'-separated paragraph, the axis-opposition line. Optional 'crown_text': a list of Great Seal crown-text entries {text, pins, clockwise}, pins = [letter, occurrence, position] triples; optional per-entry 'clockwise' (default true) picks the arc's reading direction — true sweeps increasing angle (the TOP arc), false sweeps decreasing (the BOTTOM arc) — the outer curved-text arc outside the ring band, validated and angle-solved by data.rings.validate_preset/core.crown_text. app.settings_store migrates a stored settings file's old bundled name (any generation) onto the current one. THE CROSS WORDS: DOMY and LOOP wear their cross's four station words as outside-the-band arc text like the Dollar's crown texts — the '{text, center, clockwise}' crown-text entry form, one word CENTERED per station seat (core.crown_text.centered_word_angles); DOMY carries FEAR/ANGER/HATE/SUFFERING, LOOP carries HOPE/FAITH/LOVE/SALVATION, and both carry a per-letter hover 'legend' quoting the Two Crosses stations (CUBE.md) and the owner's letter symbolism (Ysteria/Orge/Detest/Misery; Tharsos/Latria/Pothos/Opheleia). THE DOLLAR'S TWO SYMBOLIKE: every Dollar letter reads BOTH as a Double-Trinity office (Malignant Accuser, Anointed Aegis, Satanic Scourge, Omnific Originator, Nazarene Advocate, the Eye as Judge) AND as a Cube term (Megalomania, Abnegation, Storm, Obligation, Numbness). THE EYE AT THE APEX: the Dollar's 12h seat wears the Eye of Providence glyph (letter '👁') instead of G — the canonical Eye.png resolves per the Settings art source (_gem/_gpt), and the per-preset 'Shine' toggle (settings.ring_eye_shine, constants.RING_EYE_SHINE_DEFAULT — Dollar default ON) swaps in Eye_shine.png, the glory-of-rays master; see CUBE.md's Banknote Seal for the Eye's PROPOSED reading. Templar: the seal layout, all six positions wearing the templar-cross glyph, no crown text, no legend. There is no 'Rose' card — the Rose lives as the seventh POINTER (CUBE.md - The Rose of the Twenty-Four), never a ring preset. 'The One' sits on the 'octa' outer — Omega alone at the midnight/24h seat, the other seven empty fields wearing their own NUMBER glyphs (3/6/9/12/15/18/21) exactly as those number plates were made for; 'full' is PRESET-FREE (custom rings only). Every bundled preset's INNER default: DOMY/LOOP/Dollar all read 'seconds', Templar reads 'seconds_cross', The One reads 'simple_octa' (constants.RING_INNER_PRESET_DEFAULT).

12.name: M — Misery
12.reading:
Suffering — the dark path's last station: M for Miseria, Latin for wretchedness. At noon what fermented in the dark stands naked in full light — "nothing is secret, that shall not be made manifest" (Luke 8:17); and the Passion itself darkened noon: "from the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land" (Matthew 27:45).

Down the spine: Ω — Suffering against Anger; the dark path ends EXPOSED before the Judge at noon (the chiasm of the Two Crosses).

20.name: Y — Ysteria
20.reading:
Fear — the dark path's first station, at dusk on the future's red arm: Y for Ysteria (Greek ὑστέρα — the panic that seizes and unmans) and for the Yips, the fear that blocks the hand at the decisive moment. "The thing which I greatly feared is come upon me" (Job 3:25).

Across the crossbar: D — Fear against Hate, the panic of dusk facing the cold decision of the hour before dawn.

24.name: Ω — Orge
24.reading:
Anger — the midnight station: Ω for Orgē (ὀργή — wrath, the anger that keeps), at the LIVID hour — lividus is Latin for bruise-purple and for rage. Ephesians 4:26 broken: the sun went down upon the wrath, and midnight found it awake.

Up the spine: M — Anger against Suffering: what midnight wrath ferments, noon will expose (Luke 8:17).

4.name: D — Detest
4.reading:
Hate — the station before dawn: D for Detestatio, the Latin curse of loathing — anger cooled into cold, decided hate on the past's blue arm; Judas's own hour, the kiss by night. "He that hateth his brother… walketh in darkness" (1 John 2:11).

Across the crossbar: Y — Hate against Fear, the frozen grudge facing the panic that first bred it.

12.name: L — Latria
12.reading:
Faith — the noon station: L for Loyalty, the faithfulness that holds under trial, and for Latria (λατρεία), the whole service of worship — not believing THAT, but serving WHOM. "Faith is the substance of things hoped for" (Hebrews 11:1).

Down the spine: Ω — Faith against Salvation: what is served in daylight is delivered at midnight (the chiasm of the Two Crosses).

16.name: Π — Pothos
16.reading:
Love — the vigor arm's station: Π for Pothos (πόθος — the longing that moves), love as DEED and courage: the vow made, the table set at evening. "Greater love hath no man than this" (John 15:13).

Across the crossbar: Θ — Love against Hope, the deed at evening facing the seed at morning.

24.name: Ω — Opheleia
24.reading:
Salvation — the light's ending in the dark's own hour: Ω for Ōpheleia (ὠφέλεια — the help that delivers) and for Omega itself, completion. "At midnight Paul and Silas prayed… and all the doors were opened" (Acts 16:25–26).

Up the spine: L — Salvation against Faith; the light path ends REMADE in the Creator's hands at midnight (2 Corinthians 5:17).

8.name: Θ — Tharsos
8.reading:
Hope — the light path's first station, on Renewal's green: Θ for Tharsos (θάρσος — courage, the good heart), the confidence that dares the morning; hope rises humbly, the seed and the sprout. "Be of good cheer" — θαρσεῖτε (John 16:33).

Across the crossbar: Π — Hope against Love, the seed at morning facing the deed at evening.

12.name: 12 — The Noon
12.reading:
The present — the Judge's hour and the poem's first greeting: good day, TODAY. The dial's time doctrine holds that the past never existed and the future never comes; noon is the hour that says so in full light. "This is the day which the LORD hath made" (Psalm 118:24).

Down the axis: Ω — the present against The One who holds all of time; the day's height facing the deep that begins and completes it (Revelation 1:8).

15.name: 15 — The Afternoon
15.reading:
The working hour — the day's labor carried onto its far slope: "man goeth forth unto his work and to his labour until the evening" (Psalm 104:23). The card of hours needs no emblem here; the number is the work itself, counted.

Across the wheel: 3 — the working afternoon against the souls' still hour; the hand at its task facing the deep where no hand moves.

18.name: 18 — The Evening Frontier
18.reading:
Day meets night — the frontier hour and the poem's second greeting: good evening, life flowing in love toward tomorrow. The Hebrew day BEGINS at sunset — "the evening and the morning were the first day" (Genesis 1:5) — so this frontier is a beginning worn as an ending.

Across the wheel: 6 — evening against dawn, the two frontiers of the night: one closes the light, the other gives it back.

21.name: 21 — The Vesper Hour
21.reading:
The feast and the rest after work — the Rose's own hour, love's red thinned by moonlight. What the afternoon earned, the vesper hour enjoys and lays down: "he giveth his beloved sleep" (Psalm 127:2).

Across the wheel: 9 — the vesper rest against the climbing morning; the day laid down facing the day picking itself up.

24.name: Ω — The One
24.reading:
Where the count would close at 24 stands the letter that closes the alphabet: "I am Alpha and Omega… which is, and which was, and which is to come" (Revelation 1:8) — the definition of The One — with Exodus 3:14, I AM THAT I AM, the name spoken by itself. On the card of hours the midnight seat is the one hour no number can say: the hour that ends one day and begins the next is not a count but a completion. E PLURIBUS UNUM — out of many hours, one wheel.

Up the axis: 12 — The One against the noon it judges from; the deep that holds all of time facing the hour that can only hold today.

3.name: 3 — The Souls' Hour
3.reading:
The deep of night — the Ages wheel's Unborn wedge pools here: the ancestors and the not-yet-born in one moonlight community, the sea a soul comes from and returns to. The only hour awake with nothing but the stars: "when I consider thy heavens… the moon and the stars" (Psalm 8:3).

Across the wheel: 15 — the still hour against the working afternoon; the community of souls facing the single pair of hands at its task.

6.name: 6 — The New Morning
6.reading:
Rebirth without the past — the poem's fourth greeting: the finished night needs no more thought. "His compassions fail not. They are new every morning" (Lamentations 3:22–23).

Across the wheel: 18 — dawn against evening: the frontier that returns the light facing the frontier that surrendered it.

9.name: 9 — The Climbing Morning
9.reading:
Life rising toward noon — spring's own green in the Rose, the day on its most alive climb. "In the morning sow thy seed" (Ecclesiastes 11:6): the morning hour is the sowing hour, because everything it does still has the whole day to grow in.

Across the wheel: 21 — the climb against the rest; seed-time facing the feast.

12.name: ✠ — The Noon Watch
12.reading:
Good day — the cross at zenith, duty kept in full light: "walk while ye have the light" (John 12:35). Four crosses ring this card and the glyph never changes — only the hour does; the card's whole doctrine is constancy under changing light, the vigil that does not pick its weather.

Down the spine: the Midnight Watch — the same cross in all of the light and in none of it.

18.name: ✠ — The Evening Watch
18.reading:
Good evening — the frontier post where day meets night, life flowing in love toward tomorrow: "abide with us: for it is toward evening, and the day is far spent" (Luke 24:29). The order's banner was the Beauceant, black over white — a duality worn as cloth — and this is the hour its two fields touch.

Across the crossbar: the Morning Watch — the watch that hands the light away facing the watch that receives it back.

24.name: ✠ — The Midnight Watch
24.reading:
Good night — the peaceful death, full of understanding; the watch kept when every other light is out: "at midnight there was a cry made… behold, the bridegroom cometh" (Matthew 25:6). The vigil hour proves the vigil: anyone stands guard at noon.

Up the spine: the Noon Watch — the same cross, the opposite weather.

6.name: ✠ — The Morning Watch
6.reading:
The new morning — rebirth without the past: "weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning" (Psalm 30:5). The night's watch ends not in relief but in renewal — the fourth greeting hands the wheel back to the first.

Across the crossbar: the Evening Watch — the receiving frontier facing the surrendering one.

12.name: 👁 — The Eye of Providence
12.reading:
God as JUDGE — the Eye of Providence over the crown, the office that watches and weighs: "the eyes of the LORD run to and fro through the whole earth" (2 Chronicles 16:9). On the Cube this is the high seat of the judgment hinge: judgment by BOND — Loyalty in measure, Tribalism past it.

Across the wheel: Ω — the Judge against the Creator, the weighing above facing the making below (Revelation 1:8; Genesis 1:1).

16.name: S — Satanic Scourge
16.reading:
the Devil as DESTROYER — the Satanic Scourge, the force that wastes what it cannot own, on the vigor arm: where the Accuser is judicial evil, the Scourge is destructive evil. On the Cube: STORM — Vigor that has lost direction, the fall of Frenzy.

Across the wheel: N — the Scourge against the Advocate, the unmaking hand facing the defending word (the Double Trinity's Advocate ↔ Destroyer diagonal).

20.name: M — Malignant Accuser
20.reading:
the Devil as PROSECUTOR — the Malignant Accuser who indicts the soul: "the accuser of our brethren" (Revelation 12:10); diabolos itself means the slanderer. On the Cube: MEGALOMANIA — Dignity enthroned as divinity, Lucifer's own fall: "I will ascend into heaven" (Isaiah 14:13).

Across the wheel: A — the Accuser against the Aegis, the charge brought facing the shield raised (Prosecutor ↔ Preserver).

24.name: Ω — Omnific Originator
24.reading:
God as CREATOR — the Omnific Originator, the all-creating: he does not guard, defend, accuse or destroy what exists; he gives existence to existence itself (Ho On, "the One Who Is"; Revelation 1:8). On the Cube Ω is the judgment hinge entire: OBLIGATION — to whom or to what am I bound? Loyalty ↔ Integrity in measure, Tribalism ↔ Legalism past it.

Across the wheel: 👁 — the Creator against the Judge, the making below facing the weighing above (Revelation 1:8; Genesis 1:1).

4.name: N — Nazarene Advocate
4.reading:
Jesus as ADVOCATE — the Nazarene Advocate who answers the charge: "we have an advocate with the Father" (1 John 2:1); he does not deny the sin, he stands beside the sinner. On the Cube: NUMBNESS — Composure emptied of life, the fall of Lethargy, the sleeping watch (Matthew 26:40).

Across the wheel: S — the Advocate against the Scourge, the defending word facing the unmaking hand (the Double Trinity's Advocate ↔ Destroyer diagonal).

8.name: A — Anointed Aegis
8.reading:
Jesus as GUARDIAN — the Anointed Aegis, the shield that takes the blow: the Guardian protects from attack as the Advocate defends from accusation; the Preserver's own green arm (Hebrews 1:14). On the Cube: ABNEGATION — Humility turned against the self, the fall of Self-Annihilation, Judas's green fall.

Across the wheel: M — the Aegis against the Accuser, the shield raised facing the charge brought (Prosecutor ↔ Preserver).
